newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet loses $18 million as revenues sag.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet loses $18 million as revenues sag.

text.p: ValuJet Inc. said Wednesday it lost more than $18 million in the first quarter, as the airline failed to post a profit after being grounded for safety concerns last year.
It lost $18.5 million, or 34 cents a share, compared with a profit of $10.7 million, or 18 cents a share a year earlier.
Revenues slumped to $36.9 million from $110.0 million in the first quarter of 1996.
ValuJet returned to limited service last September after being grounded in June following the May 11 crash in the Florida Everglades that killed 110 people.

"ValuJet finished the first quarter with positive momentum as evidenced by our consistently improving load factor, solid operational results and strong balance sheet, including more than $138 million cash," said Chairman Robert Priddy.
"All of these factors are critical as Va1uJet moves forward with its plan to return the airline to consistent levels of profitability," he said.
The carrier said that in the first quarter, it resumed service to West Palm Beach and Fort Myers, Fla., and to Boston.
It also resumed service to Dallas/Fort Worth in April and plans to begin service to Charlotte, N.C., and Flint, Mich.
ValuJet's stock was unchanged at $6.625 on Nasdaq.
